title: Co-ordinated Sciences — Grade 10 Entrance
subject: science
instructions:
Answer **all** questions. Write your answer to each question in the space provided.

- You may use a calculator.
- You should show all your working and use appropriate units.
- The total mark for this paper is 120. The number of marks for each question or part question is shown in brackets [ ].
- The Periodic Table is provided (see the last page of the paper).

questions.prompt:
A student watches some scary movies. The average pulse rate of the student is measured during each movie. The highest pulse rate of the student is also recorded. Table 1.1 shows the results.

**Table 1.1**

| movie | average pulse rate during the movie / beats per minute | highest pulse rate / beats per minute | difference in pulse rate / beats per minute |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 82 | 122 | 40 |
| B | 79 | 116 | 37 |
| C | 84 | 132 | 48 |
| D | 80 | 123 | 43 |
| E | 86 | 104 | 18 |

The student has a 'flight or fight' response to the movies causing adrenaline to be released.

Identify the movie in Table 1.1 that results in the **lowest** average pulse rate.

Using Table 1.1 (pulse rates during scary movies):

| movie | average pulse rate during the movie / beats per minute | highest pulse rate / beats per minute | difference in pulse rate / beats per minute |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 82 | 122 | 40 |
| B | 79 | 116 | 37 |
| C | 84 | 132 | 48 |
| D | 80 | 123 | 43 |
| E | 86 | 104 | 18 |

Identify the movie in Table 1.1 that results in the **greatest** release of adrenaline.

Movie **D** lasts 2 hours. The average pulse rate of the student during movie D is 80 beats per minute.

Using the average pulse rate, calculate the total number of heart beats during the movie.

total = ................ beats
Circle the target organ for adrenaline that causes the results in Table 1.1 (increased pulse rate during scary movies).

State **two** other effects of adrenaline on the body.

Do **not** include the effect on pulse rate.

1 ................

2 ................
questions.criteria: 1 mark for each correct effect (max 2), e.g.: increased breathing rate; increased blood glucose concentration; pupils dilate (widen); increased blood flow to muscles; hairs stand on end. Do not accept increased pulse/heart rate.

questions.prompt: State the component of blood that transports the hormone adrenaline.

State the name of this characteristic.
State the name of **one** other characteristic of living things (other than sensitivity).
questions.answerKey: any one of: movement, respiration, growth, reproduction, excretion, nutrition

**Table 3.1**

| radiation | ionising |
|---|---|
| alpha (α) | |
| beta (β) | |

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:
A student investigates the effect of light on an aquatic plant. The student counts the number of bubbles of gas released in one minute by the aquatic plant kept in the light. The experiment is repeated with the aquatic plant kept in the dark. Table 7.1 shows the results.

**Table 7.1**

| environmental condition | number of bubbles of gas released in one minute |
|---|---|
| light | 32 |
| dark | 0 |

Complete the sentences to explain the results shown in Table 7.1.

The aquatic plant releases more bubbles of (1) ______ gas when kept in the light.

This is because the process of (2) ______ requires energy from light.

This energy is used to react the raw materials (3) ______ and (4) ______.

This process takes place in plant cell structures called (5) ______.
questions.answerKey: 1 = oxygen; 2 = photosynthesis; 3 = carbon dioxide; 4 = water (3 and 4 in either order); 5 = chloroplasts

questions.prompt: State the name of the response that causes plants to grow towards light.

name 2: ................

questions.criteria: 1 mark: xylem named. 1 mark: xylem function — transports water (and mineral ions) from the roots up the plant. 1 mark: phloem named. 1 mark: phloem function — transports sucrose (sugars) and amino acids around the plant.

questions.prompt: Describe the importance of nitrate ions in the synthesis of proteins.
questions.criteria: 1 mark: nitrate ions supply nitrogen which is used to make amino acids (which are joined together to form proteins).

questions.prompt:
